title: What and where Muskogee was
summary: He describes Muskogee as a town of about 30,000 with several railroads, roughly 300 miles from Kansas City and 60 miles from Tulsa.

blocks.x: Muskogee was about 30,000 population and even today, I don't think it's too much over 30. It might be 40, you know, after all these years has passed. It might be 40 or close to 40.
And what goes on there? What made Muskogee? Was it a railroad junction or something?
Well, not, it wasn't railroad junction, although they had about -- of course, during those days, you
know, they had two or three railroads running in there, you know, like -- oh, let's see. I imagine the Midland Valley, the Frisco and Katy -- K&T --
How far from Kansas City is it?
Well, I would say it's close to about 275 or 80 miles and probably during that time, it was about 300 miles from Kansas City.
What's the biggest city nearest to Muskogee?
Well, the biggest city nearest to Muskogee would be Tulsa, Oklahoma, which was about 60 miles from Muskogee.
